h: פָּרָשַׁת כִּי תֵצֵא, ט״ז Ki Seitzei, 16
Moshe’s Crowns and Rabbi Akiva’s Gate of Teshuvah

p: To understand what they said in the Gemara
at the end of eight rows"
specifically at the end of eight rows?
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, knew
on the two crowns that Yisrael merited,
and therefore when Moshe took them,
the skin of his face shone."
which is a term of light.
Only in the Midrash (Tanchuma Ki Sisa 37)
that they are called rays of hod.
do we find that they were of hod.
But it appears to be hinted
"and you shall place some of your hod upon him,"
and Rashi, of blessed memory, explained:
"This is the radiance of the skin of the face";
וְכֵן כָּתַב בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַתְרָא עה, א)
and so it says in the Gemara (Bava Basra 75a):
"'Some of your hod' — and not all of your hod;
the face of Moshe was like the face of the sun,
the face of Yehoshua like the face of the moon."
that the radiance of Moshe's face
and since it says in the Gemara:
"And Moshe merited all of them and took them,"
that the crowns were of hod.
But in truth we do not find
and "the face of Yehoshua was like the face of the moon"
that he received from the wisdom of Moshe,
who was like the face of the sun,
But the matter of the crowns
alludes to the aspect of the Oral Torah,
as is written in the Gemara (Megillah 28b):
And this is the aspect of the primordial light
that the Holy One, Blessed is He, hid away for the righteous;
and it says in Sefer HaBahir (144–150)
that He hid it in the Oral Torah.
in the utterance "Let there be light,"
this was handed down and revealed,
for they correspond to the five books of the Torah
only the light of the Oral Torah,
which is the aspect of the tip of the Yud,
this was hidden in the Oral Torah,
and this is called the crown of Torah.
It teaches that the Holy One, Blessed is He, wrapped Himself
and the radiance of His splendor shone
from one end of the world to the other, etc.
אָמַר לוֹ מִקְרָא מָלֵא הוּא (תְּהִלִּים קד, ב)
He said to him: It is an explicit verse (Tehillim 104:2):
'Who wraps Himself in light as in a garment.'"
And before that it is written (Tehillim 104:1):
"Hashem my God, You are very great";
it would no longer be called great
compared with what is greater than it;
and this is the attribute of Keser Elyon.
And after this it is written:
"You have clothed Yourself in splendor and majesty";
of which man has some grasp
for "the King clothes Himself in ten garments,"
for the creation of the world.
And after this it is written:
"Who wraps Himself in light as in a garment";
for it is the garment of the attribute of Chochmah,
"what have you searched out, what do you know," etc.,
of which there is as yet no grasp;
and this was the primordial light.
And hod is the attribute of Aharon HaKohen,
"And Aharon your brother shall be a mouth for you";
"The Torah of truth was in his mouth...
and Torah they shall seek from his mouth."
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, merited
at the time he received the last Tablets,
as is written in the Midrash Rabbah.

p: שֶׁיָּשַׁב לוֹ מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
that Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, sat
at the end of eight rows
that his portion was not in the crowns of the letters,
but only in the attribute of Hod,
which is the portion of Aharon,
who was the root of the Oral Torah,
הָיָה סָבוּר שֶׁשָּׁם גַּם הוּא יָבִין
he thought that there he too would understand,
for he too had a portion
And since he did not know
that is, even there he did not understand,
for this did not belong to his portion,
since he had never corrupted anything
until his mind was set at ease by this,
that he saw his mind was broader than theirs
(as was explained in the previous maamar).
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא בַתְרָא עה, א)
And this is what they said in the Gemara (Bava Basra 75a):
"'Some of your hod' — and not all of your hod;
the face of Moshe was like the face of the sun."
For in truth it needs to be understood:
where did the holy Zohar get
that what is said, "and handed it on to Yehoshua,"
וְהָא גַּם אֵצֶל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
After all, regarding the Oral Torah too
"And you shall come to the Kohanim, the Levi'im,
Also, regarding the halachos that were forgotten
in the days of mourning for Moshe,
who was then of the Sanhedrin;
דִּבְחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה
that the aspect of the Oral Torah of Moshe
"and you shall place some of your hod upon him,"
שֶׁהוּא מִבְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁלּוֹ
which is of the aspect of his Oral Torah.
there would have been given to them only
the five books of the Torah
and the Book of Yehoshua alone."
So the Book of Yehoshua too
and it too was permitted to be written.
And although written in it are
what is alluded to in it,
and this, which was a passage in the Torah,
and the rest of the book too
that is, the worth and preciousness
for "land" is the attribute of Malchus,
as is written in the holy Zohar:
"heaven is the Holy One, Blessed is He,
"'And of the fatness of the earth' — this is Mishnah."
And there is set out each one's
which is the aspect of the Oral Torah;
שֶׁזֶּה רָצָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and this is what Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, wished
since he wished to enter Eretz Yisrael;
and once he did not enter,
"and you shall place some of your hod upon him";
and they said: "'some of your hod'
and not all of your hod;
the face of Moshe was like the face of the sun,"
for he was the very essence of the light,
"and the face of Yehoshua like the face of the moon,"
for he handed it to Yehoshua.

p: And hadar (majesty) is the aspect of Yesod,
"The majesty of the face is the beard";
and one who has corrupted this attribute
"and you shall honor the face of an elder";
for "an elder is one who has acquired wisdom,"
and one who has merited wisdom,
who is the attribute of Tzaddik,
"Gird your sword upon your thigh, O mighty one,
and "thigh" is called the aspect of the covenant,
to conquer his inclination in this.
And he merits the attribute of hod,
which is the aspect of the Oral Torah,
which is the attribute of Yesod,
"the tzaddik is the foundation of the world."
the root of the Oral Torah
because he merited the attribute of Tzaddik,
and for the upright of heart, gladness"
and they learned from this as a matter of law
that the name Akivah is written
with a Hei and not with an Alef;
and therefore it is alluded to in this pasuk
that he merited the attribute of Tzaddik.
But from the fact that his name is alluded to
of "and for the upright of heart, gladness,"
which is the righteous to light,
to straighten the heart as well,
for he was a son of the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik;
one who still has dealings with this.
"one man who is destined to live
at the end of several generations,
and Akiva ben Yosef is his name."
Why is he mentioned specifically here
And in the Midrash Rabbah and Tanchuma (Chukas; Bamidbar Rabbah 19:7, Tanchuma Chukas 8)
שָׁמַע קוֹלוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
he heard the voice of the Holy One, Blessed is He,
with the passage of the Red Heifer,
and saying a halachah in the name of the one who said it:
So why here does He mention
Rabbi Akiva by his father's name?
that the Holy One, Blessed is He, said so.
"and it is then said in the name
of Rabbi Akiva ben Yosef just as he said it"
why did the Gemara mention him here
לֹא נִזְכָּר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּשֵׁם אָבִיו
Rabbi Akiva is not mentioned by his father's name?
that for this reason he merited
to be the root of the Oral Torah:
from the attribute of Yosef HaTzaddik,
and he merited to straighten the heart,
"and for the upright of heart, gladness,"
so that he can rectify everything
עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
through the aspect of the Oral Torah.
to be the root of the Oral Torah,
which comes to rectify the "much vexation,"
and he merited to expound the crowns of the letters,
which allude to the crown of Torah,
And because he was the son of converts,
to rectify everything to its root;
but Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
who never knew any evil at all
his portion was not in this.
And this is the matter they said in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 21b, Nedarim 38a):
"Fifty gates of understanding were created in the world,
and all were given to Moshe
is the aspect of Keser Elyon.
there shines into it from Keser Elyon
through the tip of the Yud,
And this is the gate for the baal teshuvah,
and he will repent and be healed";
and therefore the supernal teshuvah is called
to Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him;
and so it writes explicitly in the Tikkunim
the completion of the fifty gates of understanding,
וְדָא הִיא דְּלָא אִתְיְהִיב לְמֹשֶׁה וְכוּלֵּי
and this is what was not given to Moshe," etc.
"In the place where baalei teshuvah stand,
the completely righteous do not stand."
And this is what they said in the Midrash:
"'And every precious thing his eye has seen'
this is Rabbi Akiva and his colleagues."
Moshe merited the rays of hod,
which is his own Oral Torah,
and he handed it on to Yehoshua,
"and you shall place some of your hod upon him,"
And this is what the Tosafos mentioned above wrote:
עַל מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא עַל הַכְּתָרִים
on what the Gemara said about the crowns,
"And Moshe merited all of them and took them,"
that on Shabbos Moshe returns them to Yisrael,
that his level is returned to him
"and Moshe rejoiced in the gift of his portion"
he returns the crowns to Yisrael.
And then every one of Yisrael has

paragraphs.text: Source of the quoted words: Nedarim 38a — “… לך״, פסולתן שלך יהא. חכם — רב ושמואל דאמרי תרוייהו: חמשים שערי בינה נבראו בעולם, וכולם נתנו למשה חסר אחת, שנאמר: ״ותחסרהו מעט מאלהים״. עניו — דכתיב: ״והאיש משה ענו …” — “Moses was wealthy, as it is written: “Hew for you” (Exodus 34:1), from which it was derived: The waste of the Tablets of the Covenant shall be yours, and that waste consisted of precious stones. paragraphs.text: Source: Yeshayahu 6:10 — “השמן לב העם הזה ואזניו הכבד ועיניו השע פן יראה בעיניו ובאזניו ישמע ולבבו יבין ושב ורפא לו” — “Dull that people’s mind, Stop its ears, And seal its eyes— Lest, seeing with its eyes And hearing with its ears, It also grasp with its mind, And repent and save itself.””

paragraphs.text: Source: Berachos 34b — “ופליגא דרבי אבהו, דאמר רבי אבהו: מקום שבעלי תשובה עומדין — צדיקים גמורים אינם עומדין, שנאמר: ״שלום שלום לרחוק ולקרוב״. ״לרחוק״ ברישא, והדר ״לקרוב״.” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 100) — “And the Gemara notes that this statement disagrees with the opinion of Rabbi Abbahu who holds that penitents are superior to the righteous. As Rabbi Abbahu said: In the place where penitents stand, even the full-fledged righteous do not stand, …”
